blocks.text: Seth lowered the steel drum until its base touched the roof. He kept both hands on it for another moment, then let go.
It stayed upright.
Jenny looked at the chalk circle beneath it. “Right in the middle.”
“I was aiming for that.”
“I know. That's why I said it.”
He grinned at her. The first time he had tried lifting the drum, he had ended up underneath it. Today he had carried it across the clear part of the roof, held it steady and put it where he meant to.
Flaming Head hovered beside the stairwell, well clear of the wooden door. Warmth reached Seth with a quiet approval.
“You kept your attention on it until you were finished.”
Seth nudged the drum with one red boot. “I'm getting fond of finishing.”

Jenny's turn was simpler to watch and harder to count. She ran between two chalk marks, stopped at the second, then came back. At first Seth could follow her white boots. On the next run, he saw pink, a stir of blonde hair, and Jenny standing beside him again.
“Too far?” she asked.
He looked down. Both boots were behind the line.
“No. You stopped.”
“I used to need more roof.”
She was breathing harder when they finished. Seth rolled the drum back beside the stairwell. Jenny checked that the practice space was clear, then dusted chalk from her white gloves.
Flaming Head had turned toward the lake.
Seth waited for him to turn back. When he did not, Jenny followed his gaze.
“What is it?” she asked.
For a moment, there was no answer.
Then warmth brushed through Seth, carrying a feeling that made his smile fade. He could not have said where it came from. It felt like sitting alone after everyone else had gone home.
Flaming Head moved closer.
“Someone needs help.”
“Down there?” Seth went to the wall, but kept back from its edge. Between the buildings he could see a strip of Lake Erie.
“Farther along the lake.”
Jenny stood beside him. “Can you see them?”
“No.” Flaming Head's eyes stayed on the water. “I can feel something familiar. The energy. And someone very unhappy.”
Seth looked from the lake to Jenny. They sat on the clear roof beside the practice marks, looking up at Flaming Head.
“There are more like us?”
blocks.alt: Costumed Seth and Jenny sit on the practice roof looking up at Flaming Head as Seth asks whether others were changed like them.

blocks.text: Jenny had gone still, too.
“At least one more,” Flaming Head told them.
Seth tried to picture it. Someone else going about an ordinary day, finding out that something impossible had happened to them. Someone who might have nobody to ask about it.
“Do they know what happened?” he asked.
“I don't know.”
“Do they know about you?”
“I don't know that, either.”
Jenny folded her arms, thinking. “But you think you can help.”
“I need to try.”

A bus horn sounded in the street below. Seth looked toward the stairwell. They were due at Billy's office. Jenny had left the sandwiches downstairs before practice so they would not get warm on the roof.
“We should tell the others,” he said.
Flaming Head turned back to them.
“Yes.”
By the time Seth and Jenny reached Billy's office, they had changed into their ordinary clothes. Seth pushed up the sleeves of his red hoodie while Jenny put the sandwiches on the desk.
Billy had already moved a pile of folders away from the open window. Flaming Head waited outside it, his light falling across the sill. The curtain was tied well back.
Fist lay on his cushion beside the desk lamp. He raised himself a little when Seth came in, then settled with his torn cuff supported.
“Any sandwiches for somebody who didn't get to practice?”
“Several,” Jenny said.
“Good. I've been concentrating on that.”
Billy reached for the teapot. “How did it go?”
“Better,” Seth said. “The drum and I are speaking again.”
Jenny smiled, but she was looking toward the window.
Billy noticed. He set the teapot down.
“What happened?”
Flaming Head's warmth reached Seth and Jenny together.
“I have to go.”
Seth pulled his chair closer to the desk. “He says he needs to leave. Someone farther along the lake needs help.”
Billy looked at Flaming Head, then back at Seth. “What sort of help?”
“Someone else was changed,” Jenny explained. “By the energy in the lake.”
Fist opened his eyes wider. “Another one?”
“That was my question,” Seth said.
Billy drew his hands together on the desk. “Does he know who?”
Jenny waited. Flaming Head's flames lifted in the air beyond the window.
“Not yet,” she told Billy.
“Should we go with him?” Seth asked.
He had been thinking about it since the roof. If someone needed lifting out of somewhere, he could do that. Jenny could reach them quickly. There ought to be something useful they could bring.
“Let me find them first,” Flaming Head said. “I don't know what help they need.”
Seth looked down at his hands. “You found us.”
“Yes.”
“You stayed until we could manage.”
Flaming Head came a little nearer the open window, keeping outside the frame.
“And you are managing.”
Jenny sat beside Seth and put a hand on his arm. “We can keep practicing.”
He nodded. Then he turned to Billy and Fist. “He wants to find them first. He says we're managing here.”
blocks.alt: Civilian Seth and Jenny relay Flaming Head’s message in Billy’s office; injured Fist rests on his cushion while Flaming Head hovers outside the open window.

blocks.text: Fist looked at his damaged cuff. “Some of us are managing horizontally.”
Billy adjusted the edge of the cushion. “You're healing.”
“I'd like to do it faster.”
“So would I,” Billy said.
Fist glanced up at him. “All right. I'll keep at it.”
Jenny leaned forward in her chair. There was still a little chalk on the back of her hand. She rubbed it away with her thumb.
“Will you come back and tell us?” she asked Flaming Head.
“I will.”
“When?” Seth asked, before he could stop himself.
Flaming Head looked out along the line of roofs.
“When I can.”
Seth knew there was no fairer answer. He had still wanted a day, or a time, or something Billy could put in the appointment book.
“He'll come back when he can,” he told the others.
Billy nodded. He faced the window and spoke directly to Flaming Head.
“We'll be here. If you need something, let us know.”
Flaming Head's expression softened. A gentle warmth reached Seth and Jenny.
“He says thank you,” Jenny told Billy.
Fist lifted himself just enough to look toward the window. “Tell whoever it is that the beginning's the worst part.”
Seth looked at him.
Fist settled back. “Well, it was confusing.”
“I'll tell them,” Flaming Head said.
Seth passed that on. Fist closed his eyes again, satisfied.

They went to the window to see Flaming Head leave. Billy stayed beside the desk, where Fist could see without moving from his cushion. Jenny stood at the clear side of the sill. Seth kept his shoulder beside hers.
“Take care,” Jenny said.
Flaming Head dipped once, then rose above the window.
His light slid up the brickwork across the street. Seth leaned forward far enough to see him clear the roofs, then watched the small orange shape move toward the lake.
blocks.alt: Seth in his red hoodie and Jenny in civilian clothes watch from Billy’s open window as Flaming Head flies above Cleveland’s roofs toward Lake Erie.

blocks.text: There were people on the sidewalk below, hurrying home with bags and newspapers. A man stopped to look up. By the time he pointed, Flaming Head was farther away.
Seth stayed at the window until he could no longer pick him out.
“More like us,” he said quietly.
Jenny leaned beside him. “Somebody who doesn't know us yet.”
Behind them, Billy poured the tea. Fist asked which sandwich had the most filling.
Seth turned back toward the desk. His cup was waiting beside Jenny's, and his chair was still pulled close to hers.
He hoped the person by the lake would have somewhere like this soon.
